I checked the scarcity claims. Dayforce (DAY) was delisted Feb 4, 2026 after Thoma Bravo acquired it. Paycor (PYCR) was delisted Apr 14, 2025 after Paychex acquired it. The remaining listed candidates are not comparable. ASUR is a $212M micro-cap at 7.13x NTM (rebuilt), and including it moves the median only from 16.61x to 16.21x. BILL, XRO, SGE, ADBE, BL, TYL, BR and JKHY are not payroll/HCM. Padding the set to 10 with them would bias the median, which is the error round 1 corrected. I re-opened all 8 peers; every agent's figures match the StockAnalysis pages. [citation gate 2026-10-12: the StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' and EV/EBITDA figures match the pages but are aggregator ratios, which the gate does not accept for peer multiples, and the P/E is not reproducible from the same pages' own consensus (e.g. TNET 15.22x on the page vs 13.33x from its EPS). Rebuilt as Oct-9 close / NTM S&P Global consensus EPS, time-weighted by the days left in each fiscal year from Oct 9, 2026: ADP 21.54x ($270.88 / (0.723 x FY27 $12.26 + 0.277 x FY28 $13.40)), PAYX 17.01x ($103.98 / (0.641 x 5.96 + 0.359 x 6.39)), PCTY 17.09x ($153.96 / (0.723 x 8.74 + 0.277 x 9.72)), WDAY 14.86x ($186.59 / (0.312 x 11.08 + 0.688 x 13.23)), INTU 12.34x ($302.75 / (0.808 x 23.94 + 0.192 x 27.08)), TNET 13.33x ($65.45 / (0.227 x 4.87 + 0.773 x 4.92)), BBSI 16.21x ($31.72 / (0.227 x 1.71 + 0.773 x 2.03)), NSP 18.99x ($48.73 / (0.227 x 2.11 + 0.773 x 2.70)); ASUR 7.13x ($7.34 / (0.227 x 0.86 + 0.773 x 1.08)); PAYC 17.14x ($232.22 / (0.227 x 12.10 + 0.773 x 13.97) = $13.54). Core-8 median 16.61x (range 12.34x-21.54x); 16.21x with ASUR. Peer TTM EV/EBITDA was not rebuilt from filings, so it is removed from every reconciled number (the blend never used it).]

disagreements.topic: Normalized FCF base (~$500M vs ~$531M vs ~$575M) and stock-based-pay treatment
disagreements.positions: agent_2: ~$500M = TTM FCF $575.1M - $74.8M, levered, before SBC, used only to size buybacks; SBC dilution assumed offset. agent_5: $531M = TTM OCF $801.5M - $74.8M - 6% capex ($132M) = $594M, then less $63M SBC; unlevered, after SBC. agents 1, 3 and 4: $575M = the '>$650M' 2026 guide - $74.8M; levered, before SBC. They then add ~$23-31M after-tax interest and deduct SBC of 2.86-2.9% of revenue inside the DCF.
disagreements.resolution: The SBC treatment is consistent across the four DCFs. Each deducts SBC once, at 2.86-2.9% of revenue (10-Q: H1-26 SBC $31.6M on $1,103.1M revenue). Each also nets SBC issuance out of the buyback or net-debt roll-forward. That is not double counting: the DCF deduction covers dilution after Oct 2027, and the roll-forward covers Jul 2026 to Oct 2027. On a like-for-like basis (unlevered, after SBC), the three bases are ~$536-545M (agents 1, 3, 4) vs $531M (agent_5), so they nearly agree. The real error is in agents 2 and 5. They subtract the full $74.8M H1-26 tax inflow from TTM figures, but the TTM window also contains the offsetting H2-25 tax outflow: FY25 'income taxes, net' was -$66.3M against +$5.6M in H1-25, so H2-25 was -$71.9M. The net tax effect inside the TTM is only +$2.9M. On primary data, TTM normalized levered FCF before SBC is therefore $572M: OCF $801.5M (= 678.9 - 305.0 + 427.6), less the $2.9M net tax swing, less capex $226.4M (= 270.9 - 99.4 + 54.9). That is not $500M. agent_2 is understated by ~$72M; its horizon share count lands near the right value only because it also ignores ~$68M a year of SBC dilution. agent_5's OCF is understated by $72M, roughly offset by its forward 6% capex assumption, which comes from a call recap. I adopt $572M levered / ~$584M unlevered before SBC (adding back ~$12M of TTM after-tax interest), or $523M unlevered after SBC at 2.86% of TTM revenue of $2,140.7M ($584.3M - $61.2M; the round-2 text said $513M, an arithmetic slip). This matches the agents' $575M without using the guide. Upside not in the numbers: H1-26 capex was only 5.0% of revenue vs 10.6% TTM. If that held, normalized FCF would be ~$100M higher, but no primary source says it will.
disagreements.evidence: FY25 8-K Ex.99.1: OCF $678.9M, capex $270.9M, income taxes net -$66.3M. 10-Q Q2-26 R7: H1-26 OCF $427.6M, income taxes net +$74.8M (H1-25 +$5.6M), capex $54.9M (H1-25 $99.4M), SBC $31.6M. R2: income tax receivable $78.2M -> $3.4M. StockAnalysis: TTM OCF $801.5M, capex -$226.4M, FCF $575.1M (matches).

disagreements.positions: agent_2: 16.5x, 3.5% below the 17.09x median, because of the one-off debt-funded share shrink and guide-gap history. agent_3: 16.5x, because FY28 EPS growth of ~11% is below a 12.15% peer next-year growth median. agents 1, 4 and 5: 17.0x at the median, with the highest margin offset by leverage and founder supply.
disagreements.resolution: 16.6x after the citation gate 2026-10-12 (round 2 chose 17.0x as 'at the 17.09x median'). The brief requires a discount to be rigorously argued as persistent, and neither discount argument holds up. (a) The one-off 2026 share shrink is already excluded: every agent values NTM EPS at Oct 2027, with FY28 growth from FCF-funded buybacks only. (b) agent_3's 12.15% peer growth median is inflated by NSP's +27.7% (rebound from a depressed base) and BBSI's 18.4%. On the verified StockAnalysis 3Y EPS-growth consensus, the 7 peers with data have a median of 9.51% (ADP), and PAYC's ~11% FY28 is at or above it. (c) Guide-day gaps and 46% volatility belong in the width of the distribution, not in the multiple. Net debt of $702M is ~0.7x the FY26 adj. EBITDA guide, so it is not a persistent discount factor. On the gate's rebuilt NTM basis (Oct-9 close / time-weighted consensus EPS) the 8-peer median is 16.61x, not the aggregator's 17.09x, and PAYC trades at 17.14x, not 17.68x. Keeping the same judgment (no premium, no discount: at the median) gives 16.6x, 0.04% below the median. On this basis agents 2 and 3's 16.5x is only 0.6% below the median and agents 1, 4 and 5's 17.0x is 2.4% above it; their stated reasons for a discount still do not hold, but the size of the disagreement is now ~$1.5/share at 16.5x vs ~$6/share at 17.0x on the P/E leg.
disagreements.evidence: StockAnalysis statistics (EPS growth forecast 3Y): ADP 9.51%, PAYX 7.51%, PCTY 10.32%, WDAY 18.61%, INTU 7.72%, TNET 5.29%, NSP 45.24%, BBSI n/a; PAYC 17.68x on the page; rebuilt NTM P/E 17.14x and peer median 16.61x (citation gate; see comps_review).

disagreements.resolution: FY28 +11%. Net income grows ~7% (FY27 consensus revenue +7.44%, flat margin, revolver interest unchanged). FCF-funded buybacks retire ~4.1% net of shares: FY27 levered FCF ~$594M - $68M dividends - $68M SBC offset = ~$459M, at ~$250 = 1.83M shares of 45.07M. 1.07 / 0.959 = 1.116. agent_1's further haircut 'because the debt-funded shrink cannot repeat' double-counts, since that shrink is already outside its FCF-funded buyback. For the DCF I fade growth from the 7.4% consensus to 4% before a 3% terminal. agent_1's 7-8% FCF growth for six years is above every revenue forecast, and agent_3's 2.5% terminal is the outlier. My DCF is $237.1 (citation gate 2026-10-12: horizon net debt corrected from $116M to $146M; it was $237.8).
disagreements.evidence: StockAnalysis forecast (FY27 EPS $13.97, revenue $2.37B +7.44%; FY28 not shown); 10-Q (SBC, dividends $35.5M in H1); arithmetic in fair_value.

disagreements.resolution: $160. A de-rating to the lowest core peer multiple (INTU 12.34x NTM, rebuilt by the citation gate; 12.64x on StockAnalysis, x $13.97 = $172) is ordinary multiple risk, so the break must sit clearly below $172. $160 is 11.45x FY27 consensus, equal to the lowest Street target ($160) and below every close in the pre-Q2-print range ($163.96 on Jul 31 to $175.30 on Aug 4). Reaching it means the entire Aug-6 re-rating is undone plus more, which in practice requires the EPS path to break. $165 sits only $1 below the Jul-31 close, too close to the noise band. $150-155 sits near the ~$128 average H1 buyback price and would be confirmed too late to act on.

thesis_break_reason: $160 is 11.45x verified FY27 consensus EPS of $13.97. That is well below the lowest core peer multiple (INTU 12.34x NTM, rebuilt by the citation gate, = $172), equal to the lowest Street target ($160), and below every close in the pre-Q2-print range ($163.96-$175.30, Jul 31-Aug 5). A close there means the whole Aug-6 re-rating is undone and more. That most likely means the FY27 guide (Feb 2027) or a quarterly print broke the EPS path: recurring growth toward ~5%, retention slipping from 91%, or the margin step-up reversing. It would not look like ordinary 46%-vol noise. Leverage is not the trigger: net debt is ~$702M against a ~$1.0B FY26 adj. EBITDA guide.
key_drivers: FY27 consensus non-GAAP EPS is $13.97 (+15.45% on $12.10; S&P Global via StockAnalysis). Most of that step-up is the full-year effect of 10,945,515 shares bought back in H1-2026 at an average of $128.48, partly funded by a $900M revolver draw. The FY28 run rate is ~+11% from ~7% organic growth plus ~4% FCF-funded buybacks.

Normalized FCF is ~$572M levered before SBC, built from the FY25 8-K and the Q2-26 10-Q. The H1-26 +$74.8M tax refund reverses a -$71.9M H2-25 outflow, so TTM FCF ($575.1M) is not flattered. The '>$650M' 2026 guide appears only in call recaps and is kept out of the numbers. Upside not in the numbers: capex fell to 5.0% of revenue in H1-26 vs 10.6% TTM.

Valuation sits at the peer median: 17.14x NTM P/E today vs a 16.61x median for 8 HCM/payroll/PEO peers (citation gate: Oct-9 close / time-weighted S&P Global consensus EPS; the aggregator's 17.68x / 17.09x are not used). Fewer than 10 peers is a documented exception, since Dayforce and Paycor are no longer listed. The reconciled fair value of $245 (+5.5%) is 60% NTM EPS of $15.12 x 16.6x ($251.0) and 40% DCF ($237.1).

Capital return is intact: $1,655.5M remains on a no-expiry $2.0B authorization (10-Q). Supply overhang: the founder's Ernest Group may sell up to 1,090,000 shares (~2.4%) from Dec 1, 2026 to Jun 1, 2027, subject to price limits.
Event risk: the Q3 print (likely ~Nov 5, not announced) and the first FY27 guide (Feb 2027). The Feb-2026 initial guide drew a >7% drop and the Aug-6 print a +23.55% day.

Unlevered = + after-tax TTM interest (3.4 - 1.6 + 14.5 = $16.3M x 0.73 = $11.9M) = $584.3M = 27.3% of TTM revenue $2,140.7M. NTM-at-horizon revenue = 0.25 x 2,370 + 0.75 x 2,536 = $2,494M. Unlevered FCF = 27.3% x 2,494 = $681M, less SBC 2.86% ($71.3M) = $609.5M. Then +6/+5/+4.5/+4%, 3% terminal growth, 9.0% WACC: EV $10,834M. Retained = levered FCF $722.7M - dividends $84.5M (5 x $0.375 x 45.07M) - SBC offset $82.3M (2.86% x ($1,101.4M H2-26 + 0.75 x $2,370M)); levered FCF = H2-26 $276.7M (half of the $553.4M run rate = $572.2M less the extra after-tax revolver interest (4 x $10.5M - $16.3M) x 0.73 = $18.8M) + 0.75 x FY27 $594.6M ($553.4M x 1.0744). Equity $10,688M / 45.07M = $237.1 (8.5% WACC $259, 9.5% $219, 2.5% terminal $222). Blend 0.6 x 251.0 + 0.4 x 237.1 = $245.5, rounded to $245. The '>$650M' FCF guide is not used anywhere. [Citation gate 2026-10-12: round 2 had $249 = 0.6 x $257.0 (17.0x) + 0.4 x $237.8; the 17.09x median was an aggregator figure and the $753M levered FCF (= $276.7M + 0.775 x $614.8M) mixed a window to Oct 9 with dividends and SBC to Sep 30 and left out FY27 revolver interest.]
